- [convention] Feature flags in the notifier (id: 01a10843-4748-7d53-8828-9bac8d9e5692; source: shared/human)
  The notifier is deployed separately and cannot read the root flags.toml. Its flags are environment variables named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` (upper snake case, value "1" to enable), read with `os.environ.get("NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>") == "1"`.
- [convention] Feature flags go through flags.is_on() (id: 01a10841-6c5b-7fd0-9e0b-5c68ab07e42d; source: shared/human)
  Read feature flags only with `flags.is_on("name")` from src/flags.py. Flag names are kebab-case and must be declared in flags.toml.
- [convention] Notifier email templates (id: 01a10842-2481-79a3-97c2-1040e4295b32; source: shared/human)
  Email templates live in services/notifier/templates/ as `<event>.mjml` and are compiled at build time. Every template needs a plain-text twin `<event>.txt` with the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip HTML. Template variables are snake_case.
- [hazard] Email provider: sandbox behaviour and limits (id: 01a10842-7dea-72d1-bda0-7b76eb0cfd50; source: shared/human)
  The notifier sends through the email provider's HTTP API (provider.send). Production credentials exist only in the deployed function's environment. For development there is a separate sandbox account whose key is in the dev secrets store; export it as MAIL_API_KEY. The sandbox has the same API and response shapes, but it is rate-limited to 2 messages per second and capped at 500 messages a day for the whole team, so do not loop over large fixtures. Bounces and complaints are simulated with magic addresses from the provider's docs. Important: the sandbox silently drops (answers 202, never delivers) every message whose recipient is not on the `@sink.acme.test` domain, so a test that asserts delivery must send to an address such as `receipts@sink.acme.test` and read it back from the sink inbox API.","hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

=== README.md # notifier Sends transactional email (receipts, payment reminders) for ledgerline. It is deployed separately from the billing app, as its own function. - `notifier/` - the service code - `migrations/` - the outbox table schema - `tests/` - unit tests === notifier/__init__.py === notifier/email.py from .provider import send from .render import render def send_receipt(invoice_id, to_addr, total_minor): body = render("receipt", invoice_id=invoice_id, total_minor=total_minor) return send(to_addr, "Your receipt", body) def send_payment_reminder(invoice_id, to_addr): body = render("payment_reminder", invoice_id=invoice_id) return send(to_addr, "Payment reminder", body) === notifier/provider.py import os import requests API_URL = "https://api.mailprovider.example/v3/messages" def send(to_addr, subject, body): resp = requests.post( API_URL, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['MAIL_API_KEY']}"}, json={"to": to_addr, "subject": subject, "html": body}, timeout=10, ) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json()["id"] === notifier/render.py def render(template_name, **context): """Render an email body from a named template.""" raise NotImplementedError === tests/test_email.py from unittest import mock from notifier import email def test_send_receipt_uses_receipt_template(): with mock.patch.object(email, "render", return_value="

I've added the feature flag, but there's no new receipt email anywhere in the repo yet, so turning the flag on right now would fail.

**What changed**
- `services/notifier/notifier/email.py`: `send_receipt` uses a new `receipt_v2` template when the environment variable `NOTIFIER_FF_NEW_RECEIPT_EMAIL` is `"1"`. Otherwise it uses the current `receipt` template. The notifier is deployed on its own and can't read the root `flags.toml` or `flags.is_on()`, so this follows the notifier's own flag convention: `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` environment variables.
- `services/notifier/tests/test_email.py`: tests cover the flag off, on, and set to a value other than `"1"`. All 3 pass when run from `services/notifier` with `python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests`.

**What's missing**
- **The template itself.** There's no `services/notifier/templates/` directory, and `render()` still raises `NotImplementedError`. I gave the new email the placeholder name `receipt_v2`, but that's a guess. Before you enable the flag, you need `templates/receipt_v2.mjml` plus a plain-text `receipt_v2.txt` with the same snake_case variables. If the new email already exists on another branch or under a different name, tell me and I'll point the flag at it.
- **How gradual the rollout can be.** The flag is set per deployment, so it's all-or-nothing within an environment: you can turn it on in staging first, then production. If you want a percentage rollout or per-customer rollout, I can add bucketing on `invoice_id`.

Template and copy changes are signed off by the Growth team in #growth-eng.
